bull.b: Sustained revenue expansion demonstrates continued demand for Alarum’s cybersecurity and network-intelligence offerings. Although growth has moderated from earlier periods, repeated annual increases can broaden the customer base, support operating scale, and provide a foundation for rebuilding profitability over the next several quarters.

Very low leverage gives Alarum meaningful financial flexibility relative to a highly indebted business. A conservative capital structure can reduce interest burdens, improve resilience during periods of uneven profitability, and preserve capacity to invest in products or operations while cash generation recovers.

The move from large losses in 2021–2023 to near-breakeven operating profit and positive net income in 2025 indicates meaningful progress in the underlying business. While recent margins weakened, the improvement suggests the company has demonstrated an ability to move toward financial sustainability.

bear.b: The steep decline in profitability shows that revenue growth has not translated consistently into durable earnings. Near-breakeven operating profit leaves limited room for execution setbacks, while the lower margin base may constrain reinvestment and make future results more sensitive to operating volatility.

A reversal to negative operating and free cash flow weakens earnings quality and reduces internally generated funding for growth. If this pattern persists, Alarum may have less flexibility to invest in its business or absorb volatility, even though prior-year cash generation was strong.

Delayed financial reporting, alongside ongoing proceedings in Israel and the United States, creates uncertainty around operational oversight and future obligations. These matters can consume management attention, complicate investor assessment of performance, and potentially increase regulatory or financial pressure over the coming months.
